title: Session probe and stream iterator parity with ergonomic defaults across SDKs
author: Jordan Kim
release_notes: Introduce a lightweight non-blocking session probe across Python/TS/Go SDKs; standardize stream iterator backpressure defaults and retry window names; bump SDK versions (py 1.8.0, ts 1.27.0, go 1.5.3).
description:
Motivation: Teams observed sporadic mis-synced auth windows and surprising stream pause behavior when upgrading one SDK but not the others. This PR adds a tiny session-probe primitive (non-blocking background ping to validate active session/credentials), harmonizes a small set of ergonomics (stream iterator backpressure defaults, retry window names, and env var surface), and bumps SDK versions so downstream consumers get consistent behavior.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced session probe shim in Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. The shim performs a low-cost HEAD-style probe to the control plane on session acquire; failures are surfaced as non-fatal telemetry and trigger faster local credential refresh heuristics.
- Standardized retry window names to: REDWOOD_RETRY_INITIAL_MS, REDWOOD_RETRY_MAX_MS and made them case-insensitive for env parsing.
- Stream iterator ergonomics: defaulted pull-generator chunk size to 4 and added an opt-in pull-through mode for larger batched yields. Simplified the cancel-on-exit behavior to avoid subtle double-close races reported in streaming clients.
- Minor API polish: aligned Python/TS/Go documentation examples and added a compact migration note for customers who previously relied on the older STREAM_PAUSE_MS env.
- Tests & examples: cross-sdk integration test that simulates credential expiry mid-stream and proves session probe reduces observed error rate in the fast-refresh path.

Review summary: initial review flagged two behavioral edges: 1) probe frequency default was too aggressive for low-traffic clients, 2) race in Go iterator close path when context cancellation happened during a queued yield. Addressed in follow-ups: probe defaults reduced (now probe on first acquire + exponential backoff capped at 30s idle), and Go iterator close fixed by moving close signaling onto a single goroutine with idempotent teardown.

Review thread (highlights):
- Aisha: "Nice small primitive — can we make probe opt-out via an SDK config rather than env-only?"
  - Jordan: "Added sdk config exposed as SessionOptions.enable_probe (defaults true); kept env for ops teams."
- Marco: "TS reader pause/unpause semantics looked racy in tests."
  - Jordan: "Added additional gating promises and a small deterministic test; also documented the pull-through mode caveat."
- Grace: "Make sure we call out the version bumps in the migration guide."
  - Jordan: "Added explicit migration steps and compatibility notes for STREAM_PAUSE_MS -> REDWOOD_STREAM_PAUSE_MS mapping."

CI: all checks passed after two retries. Flakiness: one intermittent lint job for TS that needed a cache clear; rerun succeeded.

Merge: squash-and-merge on 2025-09-18 (merge commit b6a1f4c2).

Notes for release/ops:
- Feature toggles: session probe is opt-out at the SDK config level; ops can also disable by setting REDWOOD_ENABLE_SESSION_PROBE=false.
- Recommend monitoring the new metric sdk.session_probe.failures by client for the first week after rollout.

Longer term follow-ups called out in PR: centralized probe telemetry aggregator in the control plane (ENG-8058), and an optional pre-warm hook for Dedicated customers that want to pre-probe model endpoints during scale-ups.
